description: Where the airport card's runway sketch lays each runway, the picture runway_closure_marks places its crosses on: one layout for every app. A runway with both ends surveyed is drawn between them (NASR APT_RWY_END LAT_DECIMAL and LONG_DECIMAL, OurAirports' for a field NASR does not list), in nautical miles east and north of the field's point on the engine's flat frame (a minute of latitude a mile, a minute of longitude cos(latitude) of one). Where no runway of the field has both ends surveyed, each is guessed through the field's point along its first end's true heading (APT_RWY_END TRUE_ALIGNMENT) for its length (APT_RWY RWY_LEN), the first end where a landing on it starts; the guess is the drawing's alone (`guessed`), none is guessed beside a surveyed runway, and none within a degree of a heading already guessed (a field's parallels). Its drawn width is APT_RWY RWY_WIDTH, else 75 ft, an assumption for the drawing only and no FAA figure. A runway with fewer than two ends (a helipad) is not drawn; one with two ends and nothing to place it by is counted in `left_out`.

lat.description: The field's point, degrees north (NASR APT_BASE's ARP).

runways.description: The field's runways as the planner sends them, in the card's order.

runway_ends.description: Its ends, the first end first; the first two are drawn.

lat.description: The end's surveyed position, degrees north (APT_RWY_END LAT_DECIMAL).

strips.description: Each runway drawn, in the order asked.

runway.description: Which runway asked it is, from 0.

a.description: Its first end, nautical miles east and north of the field's point.

guessed.description: Laid along its heading through the field's point, its true place not known.

left_out.description: How many runways with two ends are not drawn, so the card can say its picture is partial.
